label: Distributions and Foliations
notes: This chapter, printed pages 490 through 514, asks when a smoothly chosen field of tangent k-planes actually fits together into integral surfaces. The whole drama is governed by the Lie bracket: planes may twist so badly that no surface can stay tangent, and the Frobenius theorem pins down exactly when they cannot.

label: Distributions as Subbundles
notes: A distribution is a rank-k subbundle of the tangent bundle, equivalently a smoothly varying choice of k-dimensional subspace at every point. Smoothness means each point has a neighborhood with k smooth vector fields spanning the planes. Keep both pictures in mind: a geometric plane field and an algebraic span of local frames.

label: Integral Manifolds
notes: An integral manifold of a distribution is an immersed submanifold whose tangent space at every point equals the assigned plane. The distribution is integrable when one such manifold passes through every point. Stress that integral manifolds need not be embedded, which is why immersed leaves appear later in foliations and Lie subgroups.

label: The Bracket Obstruction
notes: Here is the obstruction in concrete coordinates. The fields X equals partial-x plus y partial-z and Y equals partial-y span a plane field in three-space, yet their bracket is minus partial-z, pointing straight out of every plane. No surface can absorb that vertical drift, so this distribution has no integral surface through the origin.

label: Involutivity
notes: Abstract the example: a distribution is involutive when the bracket of any two tangent vector fields stays tangent. Integrability forces involutivity, since brackets of fields tangent to an integral manifold are again tangent to it. The deep content of Frobenius is that this easy necessary condition is also sufficient locally.

label: The 1-Form Criterion
notes: Dually, a corank-one distribution is the kernel of a one-form alpha. Involutivity becomes alpha wedge d-alpha equals zero, the differential-ideal condition. For our bad example alpha is dz minus y dx, so d-alpha is dx wedge dy and d-alpha on X and Y equals one. That single nonzero number is the escaping bracket in form language.

label: The Frobenius Theorem
notes: This is the central theorem. Every involutive distribution is integrable, and more: around each point there is a flat chart in which the distribution is the span of the first k coordinate partials. Integral manifolds become coordinate slices with the last n minus k coordinates held constant. Involutivity is exactly the integrability condition.

label: Flat Chart Example
notes: Watch Frobenius in action. The fields partial-x plus y partial-z and partial-y plus x partial-z have zero bracket and are tangent to the level surfaces of w equals z minus xy. The coordinate change to (x, y, z minus xy) has Jacobian determinant one and flattens the distribution into the span of the first two partials.

label: Foliations
notes: Globally, an involutive distribution partitions the manifold into immersed integral-manifold leaves: a foliation. Foliation charts are the flat charts, in which the leaves appear as parallel coordinate slices called plaques. Each leaf may meet a single chart in countably many plaques, which is the source of the immersed, non-embedded behavior.

label: Gluing Plaques into Leaves
notes: The maximal connected integral manifold through a point is built by gluing plaques across overlapping flat charts. Two plaques that overlap lie on the same leaf, so leaves are connected components of the plaque overlap relation. The notebook models this with a graph whose connected components recover exactly the global leaves.

label: Lie Subgroups from Subalgebras
notes: Frobenius pays off in Lie theory. A Lie subalgebra determines a left-invariant involutive distribution, and the leaf through the identity is the connected Lie subgroup with that algebra. On the torus, a rational slope gives a closed circle subgroup while an irrational slope winds densely as an immersed, non-embedded subgroup.

label: Overdetermined PDE Systems
notes: An overdetermined system u-x equals alpha, u-y equals beta seeks a graph tangent to the distribution spanned by partial-x plus alpha partial-z and partial-y plus beta partial-z. Local solutions with arbitrary initial value exist exactly when the bracket stays in the span, a cross-derivative compatibility condition. Compatible systems integrate; incompatible ones cannot.

label: Synthesis
notes: Pull the threads together. A distribution is a plane field, integral manifolds follow it, and the bracket measures the obstruction. Frobenius certifies that involutivity equals integrability, delivering flat charts, foliations, Lie subgroups, and PDE solvability. The recurring lesson: trust a picture of leaves only after the bracket or one-form criterion has been verified.
